Spy School

Spy School — 3 documents

Revise the sequence in the same order as in class: poster anticipation → video → text.

1. Poster — anticipation, description & hypotheses

Type: a poster for the TV show Spy School.

Subject / theme: a television programme about children who train to become spies.

Creator / source: the poster promotes the Spy School programme. Date: not given on the document.

Description: In the foreground, we can see a man and a woman. They look serious and are probably connected with the world of spies. The title Spy School and the programme information are clearly visible. We can also see the Spy School logo. In the background, the dark setting and spy-style visual elements create a mysterious atmosphere. The colours are mainly dark, with bright contrasting colours used for the title and information.

Hypotheses: We can imagine that Spy School is a TV show in which young candidates learn spy skills, complete missions, solve challenges and perhaps compete against a villain.

Purpose: to promote the programme and make viewers want to watch it. Target audience: mainly young viewers and families who enjoy adventure, challenges and spy stories.

2. Video — present & understand

Document: the video studied in class. Use the poster hypotheses, then explain what the video confirms.

Type: a video created to promote a TV show entitled Spy School.

Subject / theme: the video presents the people in the show and explains the candidates' mission.

Creator / source: it was made for the Spy School TV show. Date: not given in the document.

Summary: The video presents three types of people: the presenters, the villains and the cadets / recruits. At the beginning and at the end, we can see a man and a woman who are the presenters. We can also see children. They are the cadets / recruits taking part in the programme and training to become spies.

Another important character is a man with a gold arm called Goldfist. He is the villain of the show and an evil mastermind. The candidates have to find him and bring him down / defeat him.

The new candidates need certain qualities and abilities. They must try to be the strongest, the best and the quickest in order to complete their missions and defeat the villain.

Purpose: to promote the Spy School TV show and to recruit new candidates. Target audience: mainly young viewers who enjoy adventure, challenges and the world of spies.

3. Text — present & summarise

Type: an informative text about the TV show Spy School.

Source: UKGameshows.com. Date: not given on the extract.

Subject / theme: the concept of Spy School and the missions completed by the young contestants.

Summary: Two children train as spies and develop physical and problem-solving skills. Under the watchful eye of their spy handler, Agent J, the cadets have to solve puzzles and break codes to guide Field Agent I around London. The agents meet for their final mission: they must track down and stop the evil Goldfist. Each episode is built around a tourist attraction in London.

Purpose: to inform readers about the concept of the programme and make it sound exciting. Target audience: viewers or readers interested in the TV show, especially younger audiences.

The Recruit

The Recruit — book cover & text

For an image, remember to describe the composition before giving the purpose and target audience.

1. Book cover — describe the image

Type: a book cover.

Title: The Recruit. Author: Robert Muchamore. Date: 2004.

Subject / theme: a young recruit entering the secret world of CHERUB.

Description: In the foreground, we can see the title The Recruit and a young boy running. He looks active and determined. In the background, there are darker figures and an action / spy atmosphere. The colours are mainly black, orange and red, which create tension and suggest danger, action and secrecy. The CHERUB name / logo is visible on the cover.

Purpose: to attract readers, introduce the spy / action atmosphere and make them want to read the novel. Target audience: mainly teenage and young readers.

2. Text — present & summarise

Type: an extract from a novel.

Title: The Recruit. Author: Robert Muchamore. Publication date: 2004.

Subject / theme: CHERUB agents and James's first steps as a new recruit.

Summary: CHERUB agents are highly trained and extremely talented. They are under seventeen and adults do not know that they exist. They are sent on missions to spy on terrorists, criminals and drug dealers. Their age is an advantage because adults do not suspect teenagers. James is the latest CHERUB recruit. He is brilliant but can be a troublemaker. Before he can go into the field, he must survive one hundred difficult days of basic training.

Purpose: to introduce the CHERUB organisation, present James and create suspense about his training. Target audience: mainly teenage and young readers.

Grammar

What you need to know

The superlative

short adjective → the + adj-est
strong → the strongest
quick → the quickest
long adjective → the most + adjective
talented → the most talented
irregular: good → the best

Use the superlative to compare one person or thing with the rest of a group.

Expressing capacity

can / can't + verb
She can break codes.
be able to + verb
He is able to go undercover.
be capable of + V-ing
They are capable of solving puzzles.
be good at + V-ing
She is good at deciphering codes.
master + noun / V-ing
He has mastered skiing.
